terms.definition: A particle in the nucleus of an atom that carries no electric charge.
terms.function: Adds mass to the atom and helps stabilize the nucleus.
terms.whereItIs: The gray particles in the cutaway nucleus.
terms.whyItMatters: Neutrons are what make isotopes and add the mass that atomic weight records.

terms.definition: Having no electric charge at all — the neutron's defining trait.
terms.function: Lets neutrons add mass without ever changing an atom's charge.
terms.whereItIs: On every neutron in the model — no charge marker at all.
terms.whyItMatters: Neutral charge is why neutrons can vary freely without altering the element.

terms.definition: Atoms of the same element that have different numbers of neutrons.
terms.function: Gives an element multiple possible weights with the same identity.
terms.whereItIs: The carbon-12 and carbon-14 pair in the isotope layer.
terms.whyItMatters: Isotopes are used in medicine, archaeology, and nuclear power.
